messages:
Maria G.: FYI — early-morning spike of GPU node evictions in eu-west-1, SLOs bumped, some requests falling back to smaller models. Investigating cause and impact.
DevOps Bot: autoscaler: scale-in events=42 window=5m group=gpu-pool-eu-west-1 reason=oomScoreAdj
Chen Li: Observed NIC flapping on a subset of hosts — kernel logs show repeated reprobes, maybe firmware issue. Kicked off host reprovisioning for the worst offenders.
Luis R.: Traffic shift partially mitigated latency, but cost went up because a lot of inference shifted to us-east for capacity. Rough estimate +12% egress.
SRE Oncall: Can we document the exact steps we ran to shift traffic? Need that in the runbook so support can run it without waiting on eng.
Maria G.: Short notes: 1) set routing weight to favor us-east via config-service, 2) ramp destinations by 10% every 2 min, 3) monitor 95th latency and token error rate. I ran the CLI commands, pasted below.
Maria G.: ```
# shift 30% traffic to us-east
curl -XPOST https://config-service.redwood/api/v1/route-shift \
  -d '{"from_region":"eu-west-1","to_region":"us-east-1","percent":30,"step_pct":10,"step_interval_sec":120}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Alex P.: Helpful — add to runbook that ops must run canary for 5 minutes after each step and confirm KV cache hit rate > 70% before proceeding.
Chen Li: Root cause theory: cluster autoscaler combined with kubelet OOM eviction on pods with aggressive ephemeral storage reclaim. When the scheduler rebalanced, we saw a concentrated re-create across racks triggering NIC kernel bug. Firmware patch rolls are in flight.
Telemetry Bot: Alert summary: 1812345600-1812347200 — evictions=127, pod_restarts=312, avg_replica_set_saturation=0.84
Luis R.: Actionable ops change: add a thin-reserve of 10% protected nodes in eu-west GPU pool (no autoscale down for those), that should avoid mass reshuffles during transients. Also consider lowering max_scale_down_rate to 15% per 10m.
SRE Oncall: We should add explicit traffic-degen steps for partial-network failures: prefer regional fallback with latency SLO checks before global shift. Current runbook only has full region drain.
Maria G.: Agreed. I'll draft a runbook appendix: "gradual regional shedding" with stepwise weight changes, verification checklist, and rollback triggers (error rate > 3% or p95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive checks).
Alex P.: Also add the specific CLI for reverting weights quickly and a one-liner to restore cache priming: ```
# revert weights
curl -XPOST https://config-service.redwood/api/v1/route-shift -d '{"action":"revert","tag":"eviction-2026-03-18"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

# re-prime prefix cache for critical models
python tools/prime_cache.py --region us-east-1 --models gpt-small,gpt-medium --top-prefixes 200
```
Chen Li: Runbook update items I'm putting in: 1) add OS/firmware remediation checklist, 2) add host reprovision play (drain+reimage+validate), 3) include metrics to watch (iface_errors, link_retries, dmesg OOM/Killed).
Luis R.: Cost note for product: If we shift >25% of sustained traffic cross-region >30m, budget owner should be notified automatically. Add debounce logic to avoid noisy alerts for short blips.
SRE Oncall: Post-incident actions I captured: OWNER assignments — Maria (runbook appendix + shift CLI examples), Chen (host firmware roll and reprovision play), Luis (capacity guardrails + cost alarm), Alex (test & automate cache prime), Team (schedule chaos test simulating NIC flaps in staging).
Maria G.: Timeline + follow-ups: I'll open a PR with the runbook appendix and a short checklist by EOD today. We should also schedule a 30-min blameless postmortem review next Wed to agree on the changes.
DevOps Bot: ticket created: INC-2026-4517 — "eu-west-1 GPU evictions: runbook updates & capacity guardrails" link: https://jira.redwood/browse/INC-2026-4517
Alex P.: One last ops tweak: add an automated pre-shift step that queries KV cache hit rate and rejects a weight change if priming < threshold. I'll prototype the probe tomorrow.
Maria G.: Thanks all. Short term: protect thin-reserve nodes and lower scale-down rate. Mid term: firmware rollout + runbook appendix + automated pre-shift probe. Longer term: add regional egress cost cap to routing policy.
SRE Oncall: Closing thread — will post outcome of PR and the postmortem notes here. :thumbsup:
